rv.q: It’s a production that skilfully draws out the play’s combination of wit, absurdity and humanity.

It’s an appropriate choice for Caroline Steinbeis’s bluntly sullen, occasionally sharp-tongued production of Chekhov’s unhappy family drama. Focus is scattered in this first Chekhov play to be staged in the Wanamaker, in which the inhabitants of the Prozorov household talk at each other without taking in anyone else’s words.
Steinbeis’ bold staging pushes the possibilities of the intimate space, playing with the light in satisfyingly surprising ways.

Having seen many versions of Three Sisters over the years to varying degrees of success, I cannot emphasise how well-crafted this production is, how it adeptly captures the essence of the play while also proving so enjoyable to watch.
Caroline Steinbeis’s bewitchingly tender and amusing tender production starts and ends as brightly lit as I’ve seen this venue.
Caroline Steinbeis’ production finds laughter in even the most unexpected places.
